questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I Chose University of Edinburgh, because i had heard a lot of good stuff about their anthropology department, which was my main reason to choosing that University over others

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Edinburgh in itself is a really chill and cozy town, i really loved it. The only thing that disappointed me a bit was the low level of critical thinking during lectures.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I would say that it was rather easy. It was very easy to get the in contact with the people from the University, though the response time was a bit long.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We did not get that much assistance when we arrived, we were pretty much left to ourselves as soon as we arrived.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Consider the student accommodations, even though they might not be the most aesthetically pleasing, its a good way to find friends easily. Apply early though, to be sure to get a room

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: The distance to campus might be a bit longer but there are plenty of opportunities for public transportation

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: We had to register twice, both at the visiting student office where you had to answer a few question, and then the formal one where you had to register your arrival with your passport and flight tickets. I found the informations about these a bit lacking. They had not informed us of the one at the visiting student office which made the process a bit stressful as we had to do it in a hurry to not face any consequences.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: you could always email the visiting student office, and they respond really quick

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got almost all the classes i wanted. The only reason i did not get the third one I wanted was because overlapping courses, which you have to be aware of when applying for courses

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: do everything in good time, as the responding time might be a bit slow

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took 2 third year courses and 1 fourth year course

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I found that the teaching was a bit different. The teaching at UCPH is a bit more practical, at least in anthropology. I was a bit surprised that the had not tried to write ethnographically or done fieldwork during their BA, and only did it for their dissertation. The critical thinking was not as high either. It seemed like empirical data from the texts we read were more important than theory, which made it feel like there wasn´t a big knowledge to different theories

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Anthropology and Africa, War and Peace, Culture and Power

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: War and Peace: Its a very interesting course that touches upon war and peace and how anthropology can study these complex subjects. The lecture made the course very interesting and he was good at facilitating the class discussions as these subjects can be very sensitive to some people. I liked how war was focused on from another perspective than only destruction and death

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: The rooms we moved in to were completely empty, so we had to buy literally everything from duvets, to pots and pans

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Eating out is more expensive than i thought, otherwise its much like danish prices i would say

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There are more than 100 societies available for students, so you can almost do everything you want

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I didn´t really participate in any societies, as i felt like i made a lot of friends outside of them

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: go to the highlands, explore the city and the nearby cities, go out and eat, go to the park meadows, go clubbing

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy i would say, the scotts are very kind and friendsly

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Just start a conversation when you´re doing class discussions, or after class

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: It wasn´t really challenging, but it doesn´t really matter what day of the week it is people still go to the clubs and pubs, so be prepared to party a lot if you´re into that

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Probably the hospitality and how helpful people were

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
be prepared for a lot of exam stuff (especially anthropology) - midterms and finals have to be written while you also go to class, so it can be a bit stressful

Talk to the professors, they are really sweet and want to make you feel comfortable with talking in class even though english might not be your first language

Be open towards everyone, thats the easiest way to find friends

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just have fun and enjoy the time there

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: probably the people that i met

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Understanding the scottish accent was a big challenge in the beginning i would say

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
